question: An attacker executes 'reg save HKLM\sam c:\windows\temp\s.hive' on a domain controller with default auditing. Which Event ID combination proves the SAM hive was dumped (assuming no Sysmon)?
correctAnswer: 4656 + 4663 (Object Access Handle + Accesses: ReadData) on \Device\HarddiskVolume2\Windows\System32\config\SAM

question: You observe Event ID 4688 with command line containing 'whoami /all' executed by lsass.exe (PID 672). This is a hallmark of which in-memory credential access technique?
options: DCSync (lsass dumping its own token for replication rights)
Kerberoasting with lsass performing ticket request
Credential Guard bypass via Mimikatz sekurlsa::logonpasswords
correctAnswer: DCSync (lsass dumping its own token for replication rights)

question: An OSSEC agent reports rule 1002 (syscheck) with 'File modified' for /etc/shadow, but the checksum changed, but the file size and timestamps remain identical. This is most consistent with:
options: Time-stomping + direct kernel write via DKOM rootkit
correctAnswer: Time-stomping + direct kernel write via DKOM rootkit

question: During a containment exercise you block attacker C2 IP at the perimeter firewall. OSSEC immediately fires active-response 'host-deny' and adds the same IP to Windows firewall. This double-blocking scenario is known as:
correctAnswer: Defense-in-depth (desired outcome)

question: Event ID 4624 Logon Type 9 (NewCredentials) followed by 4624 Logon Type 3 from the same new SPN is a classic indicator of:
options: Normal TS session with alternate credentials
correctAnswer: Pass-the-Hash + lateral movement via RunAs /netonly

question: A red team runs 'wmic process call create "powershell -enc ..."'. With Process Creation auditing + Command Line enabled, the parent process in Event ID 4688 will show:
correctAnswer: wmic.exe (not cmd.exe or powershell.exe)

question: Which Event ID proves that SeDebugPrivilege was successfully enabled on a process token (most dangerous privilege for credential dumping)?
correctAnswer: 4673 (A privileged service was called) – SeDebugPrivilege

correctAnswer: False Negative (below detection threshold)

correctAnswer: Log sandwich / log burrito

options: Visible only in Sysmon Event ID 1

correctAnswer: Critical backup traffic blocked because no whitelist exception exists

True Positive – base64 is always malicious
correctAnswer: False Positive due to base64-encoded legitimate script

correctAnswer: SeTakeOwnershipPrivilege (not enabled by default even for admins)

question: You see 4624 Logon Type 2 (Interactive) for SYSTEM account on a server. This is:

correctAnswer: Sysmon Event ID 10 – ProcessAccess from lsass.exe with GrantedAccess 0x1410

correctAnswer: Attempted password policy modification (requires Domain Admins + DS Replication rights)

question: An attacker runs 'vssadmin delete shadows /all /quiet'. With default auditing, this is:

question: Event ID 6416 (DeviceGuard blocked unsigned driver) followed by 7045 (new service created) with ImagePath pointing to the same driver is indicative of:

Sysmon default config doesn’t monitor procdump
correctAnswer: All of the above

question: You see Event ID 4624 Logon Type 10 (RemoteInteractive) to a workstation from a server service account. This is:

question: Which of the following is the most stealthy way to disable Windows Event Logging without generating 1102?
correctAnswer: Set HKLM\System\CurrentControlSet\Control\WMI\Autologger\EventLog-Security\Enabled = 0

question: Final boss question: An attacker achieves SYSTEM on a DC, disables SACL on the Security log object, then clears the log. What is the last detectable event?

correctAnswer: 4662 (Access Control List modified) on the Security log object itself
